items.title: Burke details final moments as seven Iranian football team members granted asylum
items.description: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke confirmed all but a few members of the delegation were individually offered refuge as they passed through Sydney Airport.

items.title: Live: Iran's police chief says protesters in the streets will be treated as 'the enemy'
items.description: The head of Iran's police has warned Iranians against taking to the streets to protest for regime change, saying their "finger is on the trigger". Follow live.

items.title: Mine-laying boats 'eliminated' near Strait of Hormuz, US says
items.description: Donald Trump warns Iran against laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz after US media reports explosives have been placed in the vital shipping lane.

items.title: Breaking: NAPLAN testing paused due to technical problems
items.description: NAPLAN testing for more than 1.3 million Australian students has been paused following technology problems with the online assessment.

items.title: Robodebt probe clears former PM, finds two people engaged in corrupt conduct
items.description: Two people investigated over the so-called "Robodebt" scheme have been found to have engaged in serious corrupt conduct, while four others, including former prime minister Scott Morrison, have been cleared.

items.title: Live: Matt Canavan elected Nationals leader
items.description: The Nationals have elected Matt Canavan as their new leader, with Darren Chester elected deputy leader following the resignation of David Littleproud. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Bundaberg flood extent may not be known for a week, but peak below expectations
items.description: Bundaberg is facing its worst flood in more than a decade, with the Burnett River projected to peak at 7.6 metres this morning.

items.title: One problem that unites Pauline Hanson, Peta Credlin and Fatima Payman
items.description: An ABC NEWS Verify investigation uncovers a raft of foreign Facebook accounts targeting Australian users. And they're just the tip of the iceberg.

items.title: Breaking: Police return to remote station in Gus Lamont search
items.description: SA Police have returned to the family's remote outback station as they continue their investigation into the disappearance of four-year-old Gus Lamont.

items.title: Katie Perry wins High Court trademark case against Katy Perry
items.description: Australian fashion designer Katie Perry wins her High Court battle against international pop star Katy Perry in a long-running trademark case.

items.title: Report says hours of unpaid work placed on First Nations people
items.description: A landmark Indigenous-led report reveals that racism remains a daily reality for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander workers and, at the current rate of change, "it will take 118 years to eliminate racial slurs from Australian workplaces".

items.title: Financial markets 'sleepwalking into a storm' as money trumps logic
items.description: "Up the stairs and down the elevator" has been the rule of thumb for decades in financial markets — but apparently it's not the case any longer.

items.title: Asian hubs boom as Australians avoid Middle East airspace
items.description: Australian travellers are going to extreme lengths to keep their hopes of a European holiday alive despite the dire circumstances.

items.title: Australia's fuel supply struggles grind some businesses to a halt
items.description: Dozens of fishing trawlers have been stranded as a result of Australia's worsening fuel shortages, which some have described as the worst they have ever seen.

items.title: Live: Market now tips RBA interest rate hike next week, ASX up
items.description: The odds of an interest rate hike at next week's Reserve Bank meeting have surged after its deputy governor Andrew Hauser's latest comments about the Australian economy. The Australian share market continues to recover from this week's massive sell-off. Follow live.

items.title: This outdated medical practice 'reflects very low respect for women'
items.description: Outdated medical devices are being used to perform a common obstetrics procedure on Australian women that can cause a condition known as Asherman's syndrome.

items.title: Two new novels lift the curtain on what life is really like as a royal
items.description: With Queen Mary of Denmark soon to arrive in Australia and scandal engulfing the House of Windsor, royals are swamping our news cycle. So why are readers so fascinated by royal fiction?

items.title: What is behind the Greek yoghurt shortage hitting supermarkets?
items.description: Greek yoghurt has been flying off the shelves as viral social media trends spruik its high-protein benefits.

items.title: Communities across Top End face ongoing major flooding
items.description: The communities of Beswick and Daly River are both facing major flooding today, as Katherine River rises once again to moderate levels overnight. Despite this, many students in Katherine will be returning to school.

items.title: Claudia's bank let a scammer steal her savings so she fought back and won
items.description: Claudia Lee's ING savings account was drained by a scammer while she was travelling overseas — but it took 18 months for the bank to be forced to take responsibility.

items.title: Lululemon fined more than $700,000 over hundreds of thousands of spam emails
items.description: The Australian Communications and Media Authority says activewear fashion brand Lululemon sent more than 370,000 emails containing marketing content without an unsubscribe option.

items.title: SA Liberal Party candidate says 'homosexuality is not real' and 'feminism is demonic'
items.description: A Liberal candidate says "same sex marriage is not real", "feminism is demonic" and has questioned what "demonic realms" might be opened up to the world when homosexuality is accepted, in clips shown to the media by the Labor Party.

items.title: Indigenous dance academy celebrates 50 years of cultural pride
items.description: Australia's longest-running First Nations dance academy has helped to shape the cultural fabric of the nation.

items.title: Can a multivitamin slow the ageing process? Not really
items.description: A study published this week claims taking a daily multivitamin may help slow markers of biological ageing. But does the evidence match the headlines?

items.title: Evidence shows just how broken the NSW mental healthcare system is
items.description: An alleged murder by a man who absconded from Cumberland Hospital shines a spotlight on a NSW mental healthcare system that may be more broken than first thought.
